opening.text: Imagine you could call a parent at any hour, from anywhere. And every time, they pick up. They are never too busy. They listen to every word. They want to hear from you.
That is what prayer is. Heavenly Father is always there. I would like to talk about prayer.

mainMessage.text: Prayer is how we speak with Heavenly Father. We pray to Him, in the name of Jesus Christ. He hears every prayer, and He answers in His own way and time. He asks us to pray with real desire, not just words. He invites us to pray always, to work as we pray, and to pray together as families. Prayer draws us close to Him.

blocks.text: We pray to Heavenly Father in the name of Jesus Christ.

The Savior taught us how to pray. We speak to our Father in Heaven, who knows what we need before we ask. We close in the name of His Son, because it is through Jesus Christ that we can come to the Father.
Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him. After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
Therefore ye must always pray unto the Father in my name; And whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, which is right, believing that ye shall receive, behold it shall be given unto you.
Elder Henry B. Eyring of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Do Not Delay” from the October 1999 general conference.

One of the questions we must ask of our Heavenly Father in private prayer is this: ‘What have I done today, or not done, which displeases Thee? If I can only know, I will repent with all my heart without delay.’ That humble prayer will be answered.
Prayer is personal. We can ask Him anything.
He hears us and answers.
The Lord made a promise. Ask, and it will be given. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened. In our day, He said it again: draw near to Me, and I will draw near to you.

Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.
Draw near unto me and I will draw near unto you; seek me diligently and ye shall find me; ask, and ye shall receive; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ—the Master Healer” from the October 2005 general conference.

I recognize that, on occasion, some of our most fervent prayers may seem to go unanswered. We wonder, ‘Why?’ I know that feeling! I know the fears and tears of such moments. But I also know that our prayers are never ignored. Our faith is never unappreciated. I know that an all-wise Heavenly Father’s perspective is much broader than is ours. While we know of our mortal problems and pain, He knows of our immortal progress and potential.
Sometimes the answer is “wait.” But no prayer is ever lost.
We pray with real intent.

Prayer is not about saying many words. Jesus taught that heathen think they will be heard for their much speaking. We ask from the heart. Moroni taught that if we ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, the truth will be shown to us by the Holy Ghost.
But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

And when ye shall receive these things, I would exhort you that ye would ask God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Christ, if these things are not true; and if ye shall ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, he will manifest the truth of it unto you, by the power of the Holy Ghost. And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pray Always” from the October 2008 general conference.

We notice during this particular day that there are occasions where normally we would have a tendency to speak harshly, and we do not; or we might be inclined to anger, but we are not. We discern heavenly help and strength and humbly recognize answers to our prayer. Even in that moment of recognition, we offer a silent prayer of gratitude.
When we pray sincerely, we start to see the answers.
We pray always.
Prayer is not only for Sundays or hard times. Nephi taught that we must pray always and not faint. The Lord said the same in our day. Praying often keeps us close.

And now, my beloved brethren, I perceive that ye ponder still in your hearts; and it grieveth me that I must speak concerning this thing. For if ye would hearken unto the Spirit which teacheth a man to pray, ye would know that ye must pray; for the evil spirit teacheth not a man to pray, but teacheth him that he must not pray. But behold, I say unto you that ye must pray always, and not faint; that ye must not perform any thing unto the Lord save in the first place ye shall pray unto the Father in the name of Christ, that he will consecrate thy performance unto thee, that thy performance may be for the welfare of thy soul.
What I say unto one I say unto all; pray always lest that wicked one have power in you, and remove you out of your place.
President Brigham Young taught this. It is printed in Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Brigham Young, page 45. It is a book, not a conference talk.
It matters not whether you or I feel like praying, when the time comes to pray, pray. If we do not feel like it, we should pray till we do.
Pray even on the days you do not feel like it. Those are often the days you need it most.
We pray, and we work.
Prayer is not a way to skip the effort. Alma told his son to counsel with the Lord in all his doings, morning and night. And he told the people to cry out for mercy and continue in prayer.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

Therefore may God grant unto you, my brethren, that ye may begin to exercise your faith unto repentance, that ye begin to call upon his holy name, that he would have mercy upon you; Yea, cry unto him for mercy; for he is mighty to save. Yea, humble yourselves, and continue in prayer unto him.
Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Why the Lord Ordained Prayer” in the January 1976 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

Use both agency and prayer. It is not, never has been, and never will be the design and purpose of the Lord—however much we seek him in prayer— to answer all our problems and concerns without struggle and effort on our part. This mortality is a probationary estate. In it we have our agency. We are being tested to see how we will respond in various situations; how we will decide issues; what course we will pursue while we are here walking, not by sight, but by faith. Hence, we are to solve our own problems and then to counsel with the Lord in prayer and receive a spiritual confirmation that our decisions are correct.
We do our part. He confirms it.
We pray together as families.
The Lord asked us to pray in our families, so wives and children are blessed. He also asked parents to teach their children to pray. A home with prayer is a home with the Spirit.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.
And they shall also teach their children to pray, and to walk uprightly before the Lord.
President Gordon B. Hinckley wrote this in his article “Four Simple Things to Help Our Families and Our Nations” in the September 1996 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

Pray together. Is prayer such a difficult thing? Would it be so hard to encourage fathers and mothers to get on their knees with their little children and address the throne of Deity to express gratitude for blessings, to pray for those in distress . . . ? How mighty a thing is prayer.
Children who hear their parents pray learn how to pray.

story.title: Daniel prays three times a day

blocks.text: The king had signed a law. Anyone who prayed to anyone but the king would be thrown to the lions. Daniel knew about the law.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Daniel did not change his habit. He had always prayed, so he kept praying. Notice also that he gave thanks. A life of daily prayer gives us strength when the hard day comes.

application.text: First, set a time to pray each morning and night this week. Begin by addressing Heavenly Father. Close in the name of Jesus Christ. Say Amen once, at the end. Second, listen after you pray. Sit for one minute and let thoughts come. Third, pray with your family at least once a day. Keep it short and sincere.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time about a prayer that was answered. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph Smith prays in the grove

blocks.text: Joseph was fourteen years old. He had read James 1:5, which tells us to ask God. He decided to try. It was the first time he had prayed out loud.

So, in accordance with this, my determination to ask of God, I retired to the woods to make the attempt. It was on the morning of a beautiful, clear day, early in the spring of eighteen hundred and twenty. It was the first time in my life that I had made such an attempt, for amidst all my anxieties I had never as yet made the attempt to pray vocally. After I had retired to the place where I had previously designed to go, having looked around me, and finding myself alone, I kneeled down and began to offer up the desires of my heart to God. I had scarcely done so, when immediately I was seized upon by some power which entirely overcame me, and had such an astonishing influence over me as to bind my tongue so that I could not speak. Thick darkness gathered around me, and it seemed to me for a time as if I were doomed to sudden destruction. But, exerting all my powers to call upon God to deliver me out of the power of this enemy which had seized upon me, and at the very moment when I was ready to sink into despair and abandon myself to destruction—not to an imaginary ruin, but to the power of some actual being from the unseen world, who had such marvelous power as I had never before felt in any being—just at this moment of great alarm, I saw a pillar of light exactly over my head, above the brightness of the sun, which descended gradually until it fell upon me. It no sooner appeared than I found myself delivered from the enemy which held me bound. When the light rested upon me I saw two Personages, whose brightness and glory defy all description, standing above me in the air. One of them spake unto me, calling me by name and said, pointing to the other—This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!
He prayed with real desire, and he was heard. His prayer did not have fancy words. It was the desire of his heart. That is how God wants us to pray.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time about a prayer that was answered. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The church prays for Peter

blocks.text: Peter was in prison, chained between two soldiers. The king meant to put him on trial the next day. His friends could do nothing but pray.

Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him. And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison. And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
The church did not have power over the prison. But they had prayer. And it was enough to bring help from heaven. Our prayers for each other matter.

application.text: First, find one time each day when you can pray with no noise. Start with Heavenly Father, and end in the name of Jesus Christ. Second, pray for one person by name. Then do one thing to help them. Third, after you pray, pause. Listen for a thought or feeling, and write it down.

And when ye shall receive these things, I would exhort you that ye would ask God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Christ, if these things are not true; and if ye shall ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, he will manifest the truth of it unto you, by the power of the Holy Ghost. And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pray Always” from the October 2008 general conference.

We notice during this particular day that there are occasions where normally we would have a tendency to speak harshly, and we do not; or we might be inclined to anger, but we are not. We discern heavenly help and strength and humbly recognize answers to our prayer. Even in that moment of recognition, we offer a silent prayer of gratitude.
Honest prayer feeds the soul. Empty words do not.
Daily bread, daily prayer.
We eat every day. We should pray every day. Nephi taught that we must pray always and not faint. The Lord said, “What I say unto one I say unto all; pray always.”

And now, my beloved brethren, I perceive that ye ponder still in your hearts; and it grieveth me that I must speak concerning this thing. For if ye would hearken unto the Spirit which teacheth a man to pray, ye would know that ye must pray; for the evil spirit teacheth not a man to pray, but teacheth him that he must not pray. But behold, I say unto you that ye must pray always, and not faint; that ye must not perform any thing unto the Lord save in the first place ye shall pray unto the Father in the name of Christ, that he will consecrate thy performance unto thee, that thy performance may be for the welfare of thy soul.

President Brigham Young taught this. It is printed in Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Brigham Young, page 45. It is a book, not a conference talk.
It matters not whether you or I feel like praying, when the time comes to pray, pray. If we do not feel like it, we should pray till we do.
We do not wait until we are hungry to eat. We eat on time.
We also work for our bread.
A person who prays for food still plants and harvests. Alma taught his son to counsel with the Lord in all his doings. He taught the people to cry out for mercy and keep on praying.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

Therefore may God grant unto you, my brethren, that ye may begin to exercise your faith unto repentance, that ye begin to call upon his holy name, that he would have mercy upon you; Yea, cry unto him for mercy; for he is mighty to save. Yea, humble yourselves, and continue in prayer unto him.
Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Why the Lord Ordained Prayer” in the January 1976 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

Use both agency and prayer. It is not, never has been, and never will be the design and purpose of the Lord—however much we seek him in prayer— to answer all our problems and concerns without struggle and effort on our part. This mortality is a probationary estate. In it we have our agency. We are being tested to see how we will respond in various situations; how we will decide issues; what course we will pursue while we are here walking, not by sight, but by faith. Hence, we are to solve our own problems and then to counsel with the Lord in prayer and receive a spiritual confirmation that our decisions are correct.
Prayer feeds us, but we still have to do the work.
We share the table.
Families eat together, and they can pray together. The Savior asked us to pray in our families so that wives and children would be blessed. Parents teach their children to pray.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.
And they shall also teach their children to pray, and to walk uprightly before the Lord.
President Gordon B. Hinckley wrote this in his article “Four Simple Things to Help Our Families and Our Nations” in the September 1996 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

Pray together. Is prayer such a difficult thing? Would it be so hard to encourage fathers and mothers to get on their knees with their little children and address the throne of Deity to express gratitude for blessings, to pray for those in distress . . . ? How mighty a thing is prayer.
A prayer around the table feeds the whole family.

story.title: Jesus prays before dawn

blocks.text: Jesus had a busy life. Crowds followed Him. People needed Him. Yet He made time to be alone with His Father.
And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
If the Son of God started His day with prayer, we can too. A few quiet minutes early in the day can feed the soul for all that follows.

application.text: First, pray before you eat your first meal tomorrow. Say a few simple words to Heavenly Father. Second, make a short list of three people to pray for each morning this week. Third, pray with your family at the table. Keep it brief and warm.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time about a prayer that was answered. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi cries unto the Lord

blocks.text: Nephi was young. His brothers doubted their father’s words. Nephi did not know what to think. So he prayed.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, being exceedingly young, nevertheless being large in stature, and also having great desires to know of the mysteries of God, wherefore, I did cry unto the Lord; and behold he did visit me, and did soften my heart that I did believe all the words which had been spoken by my father; wherefore, I did not rebel against him like unto my brothers.
Nephi had a desire, so he asked. And the Lord softened his heart. Prayer did not change the facts. It changed Nephi. That is often what prayer does.

application.text: First, go to a quiet place. Kneel if you can. Begin with “Heavenly Father,” tell Him what is on your mind, and close in the name of Jesus Christ. Second, ask one question, and be ready to act on what you feel. Third, tell someone close to you about one prayer that was answered.
